sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN UPPER TROUGH CURRENTLY EXTENDING SWD THROUGH THE GREAT LAKES AND ANCHORED BY A VORTEX OVER HUDSON BAY WILL UNDERGO FURTHER AMPLIFICATION AS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH TRACKS ESEWD FROM THE UPPER GREAT LAKES TO NY/PA THIS FORECAST PERIOD. AT 12Z SUNDAY...A COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO THE PARENT LONGWAVE TROUGH SHOULD EXTEND SWWD FROM SRN ONTARIO THROUGH THE LOWER OH VALLEY TO CENTRAL AR AND WWD INTO OK. THIS BOUNDARY WILL PROGRESS E/SEWD MOVING THROUGH MUCH OF THE NERN AND MID-ATLANTIC STATES...AND EXTEND WSWWD INTO THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES BY 12Z MONDAY. FARTHER W...AN IMPULSE EMANATING FROM AN UPPER LOW ALONG THE NRN CA COAST IS EXPECTED TO MOVE INTO WRN/NRN MT THIS AFTERNOON AIDING IN SOME TSTM DEVELOPMENT OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN. MEANWHILE...HEIGHT RISES ARE EXPECTED ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...TENDING TO LIMIT TSTM DEVELOPMENT.

sections.title: MID-ATLANTIC STATES TO NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: 00Z NAM/GFS AND 12Z ECMWF AGREE WITH THE TIMING OF THE COLD FRONT TODAY...REACHING NRN NY TO WRN PA/UPPER OH VALLEY DURING THE EARLY-MID AFTERNOON. GIVEN THE TIMING OF THE FRONT ALLOWING FOR SURFACE HEATING/DESTABILIZATION AND THE ARRIVAL OF FORCING ALOFT DURING THE AFTERNOON/EVENING...THE FORECAST CONFIDENCE REMAINS GOOD FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERE STORMS TODAY INTO TONIGHT ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. SWLY LOW LEVEL WINDS ACROSS THE OH VALLEY TO WRN PA AND SSWLY LOW LEVEL WINDS IN LEE OF THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS TO THE HUDSON VALLEY/NEW ENGLAND WILL EACH SUPPORT MOISTURE ADVECTION INTO THESE REGIONS. ALTHOUGH MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE FORECAST TO BE MODEST /AOB 6.5 C PER KM/ ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA...SURFACE HEATING COMBINED WITH THE MOISTURE RETURN WILL RESULT IN MODERATE INSTABILITY FROM MD/D.C./DELMARVA TO SERN/ERN NY AND SWRN NEW ENGLAND THIS AFTERNOON. MLCAPE ACROSS THIS CORRIDOR WILL BE UP TO 1500-2000 J/KG WHILE FURTHER W OVER THE UPPER OH VALLEY VALUES WILL BE UP TO 1000 J/KG. DIFFLUENT FLOW ALOFT AND HEIGHT FALLS WITH THE APPROACH OF THE UPPER GREAT LAKES SHORTWAVE TROUGH...AND CONVERGENCE/ASCENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT AND PRE-FRONTAL/LEE TROUGH EXTENDING FROM VA TO E

sections.title: WV/VA/CAROLINAS SWWD TO TN/CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH...CURRENTLY MOVING ACROSS IL/IND TO THE MID SOUTH PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY...IS EXPECTED TO WEAKEN TODAY AND MOVE TOWARD THE SRN HALF OF THE APPALACHIANS /WRN VA TO NRN GA/NERN AL/. ASCENT WITH THIS FEATURE COMBINED WITH MODERATE INSTABILITY SHOULD SUPPORT TSTM DEVELOPMENT FROM THE TN VALLEY/NRN EXTENT OF THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES INTO THE WRN CAROLINAS AND VA. THE FOCUS FOR GREATER STORM COVERAGE IS UNCERTAIN AT THIS TIME..AND THUS WILL MAINTAIN LOW SEVERE PROBABILITIES.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS INTO SRN SD/NRN NEB
sections.text: A SURFACE FRONT WILL MOVE SWD TODAY REACHING THE VICINITY OF THE SD/NEB BORDER. SLY LOW LEVEL WINDS S OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL RETURN MOISTURE NWD BENEATH A PLUME OF STEEP LEVEL LAPSE RATES/EML SPREADING EWD INTO SD/NEB. ALTHOUGH MODELS ARE INDICATING MODERATE INSTABILITY FROM NEB/WRN SD INTO PARTS OF THE ADJACENT NRN HIGH PLAINS ALONG WITH STRONG EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR...HEIGHT RISES ACROSS THIS REGION AND LACK OF SUFFICIENT FORCING ALOFT SUGGEST TSTM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD BE MINIMAL. THIS OUTLOOK WILL MAINTAIN A LOW PROBABILITY FOR SEVERE STORMS...GIVEN THE FAVORABLE INSTABILITY/SHEAR...BUT CONFIDENCE IN GREATER STORM/SEVERE COVERAGE REMAINS LOW. ..PETERS/SMITH.. 08/21/2011

sections.title: NERN STATES TO MID-ATLANTIC REGION
sections.text: BUSY WEATHER DAY ON TAP FOR THE REGION. WATER VAPOR SHOWS TWO-STREAM FLOW WITH PRIMARY WLYS AND STRONG UPR TROUGH DIGGING ACROSS THE CNTRL GREAT LAKES. SEPARATE UPR JET WAS MOVING THROUGH THE MIDWEST WITH A FORMIDABLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH MIGRATING ACROSS THE MID-OH VLY AND A WEAKER PERTURBATION MOVING INTO THE LWR GREAT LAKES REGION. ONGOING TSTM CLUSTERS TIED TO THE LWR GREAT LAKES DISTURBANCE WILL CONTINUE TO PROGRESS EWD...REACHING CNTRL/ERN NY BY 15-18Z. DOWNSTREAM AIR MASS HAS BEEN MOISTENING OVERNIGHT AND DAYBREAK SATL IMAGES SUGGEST MODEST DIABATIC HEATING WILL OCCUR THIS MORNING WITH MLCAPES 1000-1500 J/KG BY AFTN. EXPECT EXISTING TSTMS TO GROW STRONGER THIS MORNING WITH ADDITIONAL STORMS DEVELOPING WITHIN THE INSTABILITY AXIS. THIS WILL RESULT IN BKN-BANDS OF STG-SVR STORMS THAT TRANSLATE ENE INTO WRN NEW ENGLAND/ERN NY BY MID/LATE AFTN. LOWER-AMPLITUDE WAVE MIGRATING EWD FROM THE MID-OH VLY WILL BE INSTRUMENTAL IN INSTIGATING MORE STORMS FROM ERN PA SWD INTO NRN/CNTRL VA. STRONGER THERMAL BUOYANCY WILL EXIST HERE AS SATL SHOWS POTENTIAL FOR STRONG HEATING AMID COMPARATIVELY MORE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER. VERTICAL SHEAR...WHILE SOMEWHAT WEAK THIS MORNING...WILL BE INCREASING AS 4

sections.title: CAROLINAS TO LWR MS RVR VLY
sections.text: ALTHOUGH STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT TIED TO THE GREAT LAKES UPR TROUGH WILL PASS N OF THE REGION...MODEST WNWLY MID-LEVEL FLOW AND DIVERGENT/DIFFLUENT UPR PATTERN SUGGEST SEMI-ORGANIZED STORMS MAY EVOLVE LATER THIS MORNING/AFTN. THIS WILL ESPECIALLY BE THE CASE OVER PARTS OF THE NC/SC PIEDMONT...ALONG SRN FRINGE OF A WEAK PERTURBATION MOVING THROUGH THE MID-OH VLY. OTHER STORMS WILL FAVOR AN OLD FRONT/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL MS/AND NRN LA. MID-LVL LAPSE RATES WILL REMAIN MODEST...BUT PRESENCE OF 1.75-2 INCHES OF PWATS AND STEEP LLVL LAPSE RATES MAY YIELD DMGG MICROBURSTS AND HAIL. WIDESPREAD SVR WEATHER IS NOT ANTICIPATED.

sections.title: CNTRL/NRN PLAINS
sections.text: WEAK MID-LVL WARM ADVECTION ALONG BACKSIDE OF GREAT LAKES UPR TROUGH IS LARGELY RESPONSIBLE FOR ELEVATED STORM CLUSTERS ACROSS NCNTRL NEB AND SCNTRL SD AT DAYBREAK. ACTIVITY WILL WEAKEN LATER THIS MORNING OVER THE MO RVR VLY. THE AFTN WILL FEATURE STRONG HEATING AND MOIST ELY UPSLOPE FLOW TO THE LEE TROUGH/STNRY FRONT OVER THE HIGH PLAINS OF WY/SD. ISOLD SFC/HIGH-BASED TSTMS WILL DEVELOP ALONG THE HIGHER TERRAIN...BUT HAVE A TOUGH TIME SURVIVING THE CAPPED LWR PLAINS THIS EVENING. BUT...STORMS THAT DO FORM COULD BRIEFLY ACHIEVE SUPERCELL STATUS WITH LARGE HAIL/HIGH WINDS GIVEN 50+ KTS OF H5-H25 FLOW. MORE LIKELY SCENARIO IS FOR ELEVATED BANDS OF STORMS /PSBLY ISOLD LARGE HAIL/ TO FORM DOWNSTREAM FROM CNTRL/SRN SD INTO CNTRL/ERN NEB ALONG THE NOSE OF A STRENGTHENING LLJ THIS EVE/OVERNIGHT. ..RACY/LEITMAN.. 08/21/2011

sections.title: NE STATES THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: A PRONOUNCED MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL AMPLIFY THROUGH TONIGHT WHILE MOVING TOWARD THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY. THE PRIMARY WAVE WILL BE PRECEDED BY SMALLER SCALE SPEED MAXIMA THAT ARE NOW APPROACHING/CROSSING THE CENTRAL/SRN APPALACHIANS. AT THE SURFACE...A CYCLONE WILL DEEPEN ACROSS SW QUEBEC AS A TRAILING COLD FRONT MOVES SEWD INTO KY/WV/PA/NY BY LATE AFTERNOON. A LEE TROUGH WILL ALSO PERSIST FROM ERN NY TO CENTRAL VA AND THE CAROLINA PIEDMONT. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S ARE SPREADING NWD ALONG AND E OF THE LEE TROUGH INTO SE NY...AND VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT THE STRONGER SURFACE HEATING WILL OCCUR FROM S CENTRAL/SE PA SWD INTO VA. MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS SHOW THE POTENTIAL FOR AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 1500 J/KG IN E/SE NY TO 3000 J/KG INVOF CHESAPEAKE BAY. CONVECTIVE INHIBITION WILL ALSO BE REMOVED AS TEMPERATURES WARM FROM THE LOW 80S N TO NEAR 90 F...AND ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT WILL BECOME LIKELY BY EARLY AFTERNOON FROM CENTRAL/ERN PA INTO VA. STORM COVERAGE AND DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE AUGMENTED BY THE APPROACH OF THE LEAD AND PRIMARY MIDLEVEL TROUGHS...WITH THE ENVIRONMENT EXPECTED TO BECOME FAVORABLE FOR O

sections.title: NEB AREA THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A FEW SLIGHTLY ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING THIS MORNING ACROSS CENTRAL NEB IN A REGION OF DIVERGENCE ASSOCIATED WITH THE RIGHT ENTRANCE REGION OF THE UPPER JET. THIS CONVECTION SHOULD BEGIN TO DIMINISH BY MIDDAY/EARLY AFTERNOON...THOUGH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL COULD OCCUR BEFORE THEN. OTHERWISE...ADDITIONAL ELEVATED STORMS SHOULD FORM AGAIN LATER TONIGHT AS THE LLJ AND WAA INCREASE. FARTHER W...A SURFACE WARM FRONT WILL CONSOLIDATE TODAY FROM NW KS INTO WRN NEB. THOUGH LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE NEGLIGIBLE THIS AFTERNOON...THE THERMODYNAMIC AND VERTICAL SHEAR ENVIRONMENTS WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SOME RISK OF ISOLATED LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS IF A STORM OR TWO MANAGES TO FORM ALONG THE BOUNDARY. ..THOMPSON/ROGERS.. 08/21/2011
